3. Earlier to the institution of the instant suit the plaintiff filed an application for redemption on 4-6-1973 under section 95(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act being Miscellaneous Case No. 78 of 1973 but the said case was dismissed by the Circle Officer Narayanganj on 16-10-1973. Against the said order the plaintiff filed a Writ Petition No. 395 of 1973 but Rule in the said Writ petition was discharged holding that the transaction as being past and closed and not attracted by the provisions of President's Order 88 of 1972. 

 4. The defendant-petitioners filed a joint written statement in the suit and denied the claim of the plaintiff contending, inter alias, that Kazi Shamsuddin Ahmed as owner of the suit land sold that same to Md Asgar Hossain. In the suit land a Duchala Tin Shed was standing thereon which was also sold to Md. Asgar Hossain Khandker, the predecessor of the defendants, on 14-10-1967 at Taka 3,000. On the same day the purchaser Asgar Hossain Khandker executed and registered agreement stating that if he gets back the consideration money by Bhadra 1376 BS he would recovery the same to the seller. But Kazi Shamsuddin Ahmed failed to pay back the consideration money and he accepted a further amount of Taka 1,600 on 25-11-1967 and 19-12-1967 and relinquished his right of repurchase and returned the deed of agreement. The plaintiff tried to get back the suit land by filing an application under President's Order No. 88 of 1972 but the same was rejected. The transaction in between the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants was a conditional sale and not a mortgage and since the predecessor of the plaintiff has relinquished his right of repurchase there is no cause of action to file the suit and played for dismissal of the suit. 

 5. Pending the suit, the defendant-petitioners filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint stating that the transaction has already been found past and closed and, as such, no suit lies. Also stated that since the suit in question was with a condition to repurchase the claim of the plaintiff that they are entitled to get back property within 60 years from the date of transfer is not tenable and thus the plaintiff's suit is liable to be rejected. The plaintiff filed written objection to the said application under Order VII, rule 11 of the CPC stating, inter alia, that the petition is not maintainable in law. From a plain reading of the plaint of the suit it would appear that the plaintiff has a prima facie case, which needs adjudication after considering the facts, stated therein. The plaint and the materials which are mixed question of law and facts. The matter in issue can only be decided at the trial on taking evidence and prayed for rejection of the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and to decide the matter on merit. 

 9. Perused the provisional application along with the Lower Court's record. Perused the findings of the judgment of the appellate Court reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. I have gone through the impugned judgment minutely and found that the appellate Court rightly found, reasonable based in rulings, that the question of limitation in a suit is a mixed question of law and facts which can be decided only at the time of trial on taking evidence. From the plaint of the suit it also appears that facts stated in the plaint made out a prima facie case and to decide such facts, circumstances needs a decision on merit after taking evidence and rejection of plaint without recording evidence and without considering the facts after taking evidence is not sustainable. It is the settled principle of law that disputed question cannot be decided at the time of considering an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It appears that none of the ingredients provided under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure are present in this case. In such circumstances of the case, plaint cannot be rejected which is supported by decisions of our Court reported in 32 DLR (AD) 235 and 34 DLR (AD) 237.
